exposure: Maternal factors (age, allergic history, pre-pregnancy BMI, parity, Secretor phenotype, Lewis phenotype, delivery mode)
Lactation stage (1-5 days, 8-14 days, 4 weeks, 6 months postpartum)
outcome: Neutral human milk oligosaccharide (HMOs) variability and concentrations
cohort: The study recruited healthy Chinese mothers and their full-term infants.
finding: The study found that Secretor phenotype and lactation stage significantly influenced most neutral human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), and specific HMOs concentrations were associated with maternal age, allergic history, pre-pregnancy BMI, parity, infant gestational age, and gender.
mod_finding: Delivery mode was found to be associated with concentrations of specific human milk oligosaccharides.
